text_fidelity_a:
Stansport Survival Bottle Emergency First Aid Kit Sturdy cup with attached twist off lid. Stuffed inside is:
--ONE red medical bag with a variety of bandages, an empty zip lock bag, 4 alcohol wipes (fresh, plenty wet enough to wipe down fingers, phone, and keyboard), 2 sting relief pads, and a large triangular bandage. The little red medical bag has zipper closure, and has a mesh pocket on outside. This was hard to get out of the cup.
-- ONE mylar emergency blanket in zip lock bag. Also a challenge to wrangle out from cup
--ONE Pen light with clip, which needs 2 AAA batteries (non included)
--ONE Large, bright orange whistle that works with ease. Attached (cheap) carrying strap. One end has a working compass (it works, and is accurate. Mine anyway). One end can be twisted off to store smaller items. Nothing comes with it inside. I stuck my pinky finger in and didnt reach the end, so matches and such would be good.
-- ONE tea light. Appears to be a 4 hour (max) tea light.
--ONE basic but sturdy multi-tool in a black canvas sheath. Includes a key ring
-- ONE chemical body warmer. If it works, then it is a really nice addition. Can be used for pain, and can be used for added body warmth. I rely greatly on these warmers, and find them a must have for any emergency kit.
--ONE D-ring carabiner. Nice addition but it is super basic and cheap, really should have gone with something of more functional size. Dont rely on this. Anything would be better. Doesnt even work to hold the cup to a bag. Just too small, and will likely break.
--ONE fire starter stick
--and, ONE sturdy cup. Just a cup, will need to supply your own filtering if that is what you run up against. The twist cap has a reflective appearance. I can see myself, hence using this as a crappy mirror if needed. Not for vanity, but maybe I have something on my face or in my eye. Not sure if it would be enough for reflection in a signal, but its possible in a low key way.

If just using it for holding all this stuff, know that there is a little extra room for additional personalization. I'd add in a packet of pain reliever, an electrolyte powder (I buy tear off sticks for convenience), a nutrient dense snack- packet of peanut butter, maybe and a fruit/nut bar? water filtration tablets. Petroleum based chap stick. Possibilities are endless, so just think through a potential situation and work up from there. I want to be warm, dry, hydrated, and preferably fed, and be able to make some noise.

Overall a fair compilation. As with any survival gear, it comes down to the individual needs and ability to use said items. Also, there is so much variety out there, that pin pointing what to have or not to have is subjective. This gives a decent foundation of items. I'll put this in my car, or add to my every day carry bag. I personally like the addition of the chemical body warmer. That paired with the blanket will make all the difference in comfort. The whistle and compass (with additional storage) is the item I am most pleasantly surprised with. Some whistles take a lot of oomph to get sound, which isnt helpful if it is something you need in a dire situation. That and the compass is actually accurate and works quickly. I have purchased similar items and have had the compass not read correctly. No good if it isnt accurate! This is good. Penlight is nice addition. Just be sure to add batteries if you dont see any in your cup.

Minor differences from product picture and product description. The picture shows a pack of batteries, mine did not have any. The product description doesnt mention them at all (not even a reminder that we will need them). The fire starter stick is different, I think mine is better than what is shown in picture. Picture shows 2 body warmers, and product description says 1. My cup has 1.

As for getting everything back in once I got it out? Eh, with some finesse, yes.

4 stars. (could have been 5 if the product pictures, product description, and what I have in hand lined up- the differences may make or break someone buying choice. Again, overall I think it is a decent set that I got). $29 is reasonable price at time of review in 05/2022
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Survival Bottle Emergency First Aid Kit

Jeff & Aimy Women's Lightweight Cotton Bucket Beach Sun Hats Ponytail Hole Wide Brim UV Protection Foldable Travel Fishing Sunhats Gray I am reviewing the Jeff & Aimmy Cotton Vucket Hat in the color " Black#990022", which is gray with a black bow. I was supposed to receive the hat in black ( 00707_black), so that it was may come up under my review. I will include pics of the hat on.

Before you select one, make sure to take a look at the sizing. There are TWO sizes available, Medium OR Large. There is no elastic, nor ability to adjust, so choose wisely.

Medium fits 55-58CM (22.2"-22.8");
Large fits 58-61CM (23.03"- 24.0") ----my head measures 23.75", this fits very well.

Despite that the product description states that the hat is adjustable, it is NOT. The only portion that is "adjustable" is the optional chin strap. On mine, it can be kept clipped on, or taken off. There is a toggle to make it tighter against the face, or allow it to be loose.

The interior has what appears to be an elastic band, but it is not elastic. It's purpose is more like that of a sweat band or to provide some grip, but it doesn't not stretch. This will either fit, or it won't.

I normally like Jeff & Aimmy products, and overall I like this too. I just want to see a cleaned up, more accurate description. (and what are with all the reviews for this product yet are for something not being sold here?)

The material is soft, light. The brim is long but can be folded back some as needed.
The slit for the pony tail is subtle. So it will blend in when not in use. But to use it, is a little awkward as you will have to feed the pony tail through a narrow slit. Not bad though. Doable.

I do appreciate that there are size offerings for larger heads. It is rare- extremely- that I find a womens hat that fits anything above 22.5". MY cranium is 23.75", so I can't wear most stuff. SO unless you have a bigger head like mine, you will most likely be wanting a medium. If your "large" is too big, then you ordered the wrong size as the size large is accurate (23.03"- 24.0"). It will just fit if your head it 24". Might be snug. It fits mine just right at 23.75". Or if your medium is too small.. then again, likely wrong size. selected. Either way, make sure you got what you ordered.

I use sun hats (when I can find them in my size) a lot. I prefer to avoid the sun. I keep it off my face and body, especially during the summer months. Between sun sensitive meds, rosacea, and just wanting added protection from UV rays, a sun hat is a great thing to have. Since I can add this to my list of companies that sell larger sized hats I will possibly be back to purchase more. I like the overall look (even if I did get something different than anticipated).
text_fidelity_b: Jeff & Aimy Women's Lightweight Cotton Bucket Beach Sun Hats Ponytail Hole Wide Brim UV Protection Foldable Travel Fishing Sunhats Gray

Viper Dead-On Tournament Bristle Steel Tip Dartboard Set with Staple-Free Bullseye, Metal Triangular Spider Wire for Reduced Bounce Outs and Increased Scoring; High-Grade Self-Healing Sisal Board The dead-on viper sisal fiber dartboard is a classic dartboard that you will likely see in your local bar or pub. The spider, or the metal that separates the segments (numbers and colors), is angled on each side. Therefore, if a dart barely hits the side of the spider then it will be directed to hit the sisal fibers. The angled spider helps reduce the number of bounce backs. However, you should notice that the spider has "staples" that go over the metal bar on both sides. If you do not like this aspect of the dartboard then you can spend an extra $10-$15 bucks and upgrade to the viper spider dartboard. Either board is a great addition to your home game room or man (or woman) cave. Great board. Made in Taiwan.

text_fidelity_a:
Iron Crush Best Hand Grip Strengthener, A Forearm Wrist & Finger Exerciser, Set of 3 Level Resistance, 2 Year Warranty, Perfect Trainer 4 Rehabilitation & Athletes, The Grippers U R Looking 4! I LOVE this set in comparison to the many other grip exercisers I have used over the years and LIKED. I use grip exercisers to relieve tension, to maintain forearm and wrist and finger strength and to work finger joints and tendons. Just in the last three months I have purchased and used (and reviewed for Amazon customers) Theraband graduated twist bars, graduated 'egg' grip and finger exercisers and now these. In the past I have made regular use of Theraband's silicone band powered frame grippers, the spring-powered 'pliers' type grippers and the brass instrument-type finger tip plunger exercisers. Shoppers will get satisfactory results from any of these options provided they are made by a quality manufacturer.

I agree with another reviewer that a choice of one of these Iron Crush grippers is easy to 'take along' in a pocket or to pull out of a desk for workday use where the mind and eyes are occupied and the hands are free. The Chinese silicon is of good quality and, due to differences in formulation, each ring does have a noticeable difference in resistance. Cleaning/sanitizing these rings is easily done. Differences in resistance hold up after each ring has been 'warmed up' by repeated use. Just like with dumbbells, start with the lowest resistance for a few reps and move up! Since I'm also offering comparisons, the silicone eggs offer beginners' graduated resistance and this set picks up where they leave off. These will not 'snap' like the rack-mounted silicone band exercisers. I often have to replace one or another band unexpectedly. As an exercise suggestion, take the 50 lb. resistance ring and link the fingers of both hands and do a compression exercise by pressing your palms together. This is a more practical use of these devices than finger 'extension' exercises suggested on the packaging. Guys and Gals with normal hands will have difficulty fitting more than two fingers and a thumb in the doughnut hole on these items!
text_fidelity_b: Iron Crush Best Hand Grip Strengthener, A Forearm Wrist & Finger Exerciser, Set of 3 Level Resistance, 2 Year Warranty, Perfect Trainer 4 Rehabilitation & Athletes, The Grippers U R Looking 4!

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail Where I live it is important to have back up food sources. Sometimes we get severe weather and that can mean an inability to go to the grocery store, no electricity, or sometimes snowed in for a while. I always try to have some different foods on hand that are easy to fix for such times as that, but one thing I have not had is vegetables for long term storage, should we have to go through an extended time of roughing it.

WHAT IS THIS COLLECTION LIKE?
WHAT SIZE BUCKET?
First of all, it comes in a four gallon sized bucket which is square. That means it will fit on the shelf more easily and be easier to stack. This baby was SEALED tight. It has a tab that you pull which starts a plastic strip coming off from around the entire rim of the bucket. The size is 13 1/2 inches high and 10 inches square.

HOW WAS THIS BUCKET TO OPEN?
I have to say that this bucket was VERY difficult to open. If you are older, or have a weak grip, this might be very difficult to open- especially in an emergency. Of course, being hungry might motivate you enough to push through, but honestly, I am pretty strong and this particular bucket was so hard to open I had to get pliers and then pull with all of my might many times to work it off of the bucket.

WHAT IS THE BUCKET LIKE INSIDE?
Inside the rim is a rubberized seal. I would assume that the way this was sealed that it would withstand reasonable water around it- perhaps not for a really long time, but enough to keep the contents dry for a bit should you need to be in the rain or have a flood in your storage area. There is a little crunched up bunch of powder inside which I am thinking was at one time a moisture control tab, but I can not say for sure.

There is a bit more space in the bucket so that you could keep other freeze dried pouches in here, or perhaps plastic dishes or other things you want to put in with it for saving space, such as vacuum sealed spices, or other mixes you might have accumulated or made. It is important that they are sealed, however as you don't want to have bugs get into the bucket over time from just loosely bagged foods. Also I would avoid grains in a bucket like this as they can still hatch bugs which will eat through vacuum sealed bags- ask me how I know..

WHAT IS IN THE BUCKET?
This is where I was a bit disappointed. The outside clearly lists what is in the bucket, but for the price, I expected to have a little better quality than this. There are metallic bags in this bucket most of which are vacuum sealed. Two of them are not, however. One of them is onions, but the other was not even labeled. It turned out to be potatoes, but there was not anything on the bag at all to indicate that it was potatoes. I would have thought that it would be labeled and vacuum sealed for the onions and potatoes. Perhaps there is a reason why they are not.

HOW PRACTICAL IS THIS KIT?
This kit has 109 servings in it. That is a lot, but the problem is that each package of vegetables is the entire contents of the bucket. For instance, it might have 15 servings of peas in one pouch, but let's say you do not want to have peas all of the time. Perhaps you have a quick emergency for a few days and then it is over. The problem is that once you open the bag of peas, the shelf life goes down quickly.

So, once you open a bag, you have to finish it in a reasonable amount of time and keep ti sealed in a jar perhaps for longer storage. It will NOT last 20 years as advertised however once opened.

HOW IS THIS KIT BEST USED?
This kit is best used as a 1 week supply for food. A few weeks at best. That means if you buy this kit, then you will have to plan on using what is inside all at once- at least each vegetable that you open. That means you should buy multiple packs if you want to have a long term storage that you can rely on over an extended period.

DRAWBACKS
I would have liked to see the pouches broken down in thirds or even halves. That way if you open one, you still have another for future use, up to 20 years. I also was not sure why the potatoes and onions were not vacuum sealed and why the potatoes are not labeled. They are a part of the kit, so they should have been labeled like the rest of the bags in the bucket.

QUALITY
The vegetables tasted good- they are freeze dried which means that you can eat them as a crunchy snack food without breaking your teeth as you would with dehydrated food. You can also cook with them, but honestly they were so good as snacks that is how we enjoyed them. It is important that you drink plenty of water when eating freeze dried foods, however. We would always have them right out of the bag at our house which is the best way to have the most nutrients.

I love that this has no added sugar or other ingredients like most "survival" food does. It is just vegetables and that fits our family perfectly as we do not eat sugar or highly processed foods.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although the bucket is very difficult to get into (at least this one was), the food inside is well protected from weather and elements. The food is sealed in large bags of each type, so you need to use up what you open in a reasonable amount of time. Not all of the bags were vacuum sealed and one was not marked, so I give this four stars for that.

As for the purchase and having it handy, it is an excellent kit to have on hand, especially if you live in an area that is prone to severe weather. I would reiterate that it would be best to have a collection of these handy as this one will only feed a small family for a short period of time.

I will update with more information should I have anything else to report in the future.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail

Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden I have been trying to get various bug zappers to bring with my family when we go to areas that are not close to a plug. This one is interesting. Let's take a look.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a small box with instructions.

CLOSED
Closed this is used for a light. It has brighter white light, dimmed light and a warning red light.

OPEN
Open this has the ability to zap bugs.

HOW WELL DOES THIS PERFORM?
This performs well as a light, but as a bug zapper, it really is not the season for heavy bugs like we will be having later in the season. I have not been able to catch the few tiny moths in the house, nor the few tiny fruit flies. That is no surprise, however, because this zapper is not very big and these guys have been all over the house.

The light part is nice for using when necessary to see at night. During power outages it also will be handy.

HOW THIS RUNS
This runs not only on USB charging,, but also works with AAA batteries(3) which don't come with it.

CHARGE TIME
This took a couple of hours to charge up fully and it lasts a few hours depending on how it is used. I usually charge after that, so I have not let it run completely down yet.

CAN IT HANG FROM CENTER OF TENT?
This does make a good light for hanging from the center of the tent when you want to see with an overhead light. It also would do well in that position as a bug zapper. It has a handle so you can twist tie it to the loops.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For using at a camp site or on a deck in summer, this is a nice little light to have at the table at night, or use for walking at night around a camp site. As for bug zapper, in the tent, I would have to have some eye masks to sleep with. The light would be too bright for me to sleep with.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If this turns out to be a bug zapping wonder, I will stop by and update my rating on this zapper/light. As it is now, it works, seems to do what it is supposed to do, but situations are not dire enough to see how good it really is.

Empower Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. [[ASIN:B001O0EG7S Empower 10-Pound KettleBell with DVD]]

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can I'm buying calories. I am buying calories to tuck away for use after all other calories have been consumed. I have this and know it is available. I dont need to worry about it. It is there as part of my "calorie savings account". Not worried about taste, not worried about anything other than calories- preferably a variety of flavors with a good ratio of macros (fat, protein, carbohydrates). Emergency food is what it is, and what it will be. With increasing prices, todays caloric purchase is a savings over tomorrows.

So no, I haven't tried it. I HAVE used other Augason Farms products for daily life use and have been pleased. I regularly buy Augason Farms (best price point, best sales). I have tried those items only because the sale price was better than buying non emergency packed food items. I use a lot of tomato powder, dehydrated vegetables, protein crumbles, etc.. and once in awhile a sale will work in my favor. That is when I will buy 2 of something. One for now, one for way later. Rinse and repeat.

Certain food items have at least 25 year shelf life, some items are 10 years. No matter, I will eat it all 30 years down the line if need be. Foods dont just go "bad". The date is not a safety issue. It is a quality issue. So maybe the smell, taste, texture, or vitamin content alters a little over time, but it is still edible. Calories are still there.

If you want to be sure of a tasty meal that is within the best by date range, then simple stack your pantry with foods that you know and love. Rotate. Have a "working pantry" that you grab from on a daily basis, then have a "storage pantry" that works as your own in home "store". It also serves as your emergency preps. When you need to pull from your storage pantry, be sure to replace. Keep adding to it, one or two cans at a time. one or two bags of something at a time. Emergency food does not need to be emergency packaged food (prices are higher for the packaging, uniformity, processing etc). If "emergency" packaged food is outside your budget, then dont bother. If it is something you are keen on, then look for sales regularly (maybe daily) and buy when the good price strikes. Of course, you can look into creating your own long term storage meals too (mylar, oxy absorbers, pails, etc).

Just.. have something. Dont be someone who has bare shelves and scoffs at preparedness because emergency meals taste bad. Nah, buy what is good to you, buy what is affordable to you, buy basic stuff or buy fancy emergency stuff. But have stuff. Prices aren't coming down, prices will continue to go up, food will be harder to come by. So at the very least consider it an investment. And if there is a true need for it in terms of *vaguely gestures around* all else that is going on (weather events, political events, ww3, etc) then you wont be scrambling, begging off neighbors, stealing, etc.

So current $60 for nearly 20,000 calories of a variety of food? Not too shabby in light of everything. (same $60 can buy a lot more calories, but be sure to store well for max "freshness").
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can

text_fidelity_a:
Xcellent Global LED Camping Lantern Collapsible Flashlight Led Light Ultralight Waterproof Outdoor Lights with 3 Modes (Strong, weak, Strobe) for Fishing Hiking Camping Emergency (Green) LD047G I remember my father using a camp lantern on a trip to the mountains one time when I was young. It required a liquid fuel and it had a mesh wick that eventually disintegrated and needed to be replaced. That was a long time ago. Many lanterns now are much different. This one is a pop-up lantern with batteries for its fuel cells and it works very well, not just as lantern but also as an emergency flashlight when help properly.

Out of the box this lantern comes compressed and it is small enough to be palmable (approximately 3” in diameter and 2” high). This is great for packing and it stows very easily in camping gear, a suitcase or even a fishing tackle box. When “opened” it stands about 5” tall and reveals a white mesh that covers the spring that connects the top and bottom halves of the lantern.

The top of the lantern screws off to reveal the batter compartment. This particular lantern takes 3 AA batteries. When installed the batteries do add appreciable weight to the lantern but this is relative; even with the batteries installed the lantern still weighs less than a pound.

There are three modes of light with this lantern – bright, brighter and flashing. The lower brightness is still bright enough to light up a small room sufficiently for navigating in the dark. Where it gets interesting is that the lantern has a small lens on the bottom and when the light is on it sends out a beam from the lens. The lens covers the internal LED so this works like a flashlight. When expanded, the lens is farther away from the LED and the result is a more diffused and dimmer circle of light under the lantern. When the lantern is collapsed, though, it creates a bright and focused circle of light that is bright enough to serve as a very bright flashlight.

The lantern has a small loop handle so it can easily be hung by a hook or a branch.

It came in handy recently when we had a heavy thunderstorm. This lantern was sufficient to provide light when the power went out. It was a brief outage but it was enough to demonstrate the usefulness of the light in an emergency.

This is a nice, compact little lantern and it works well for me. It is very lightweight and it casts a lot of light. While good for camping and outdoor activity, it also works well as an emergency light source and also a very bright flashlight.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Xcellent Global LED Camping Lantern Collapsible Flashlight Led Light Ultralight Waterproof Outdoor Lights with 3 Modes (Strong, weak, Strobe) for Fishing Hiking Camping Emergency (Green) LD047G

text_fidelity_a:
Tresda Camping Lantern Rechargeable, 370LM Dimmable LED Vintage Battery Powered Lanterns, Waterproof LED Retro Camping Lights for Camping, Power Outages, Hurricane, Outdoors, Home Décor I'm very pleased with this camping light. The design mimics an old school lantern. To my eye is a far more attractive design than the typical LED lantern. The body is plastic, but it's a good quality plastic that has a nice, solid feel to it. The army green housing is nicely complemented with a bamboo surround on the base. The rope handle is functional and attractive. The cage and hanging points are metal. The USB charge port has a silicone cap to keep water/dirt out. The cap is tethered to the body so it won't get lost.

Controls are simple: a single knob that turns it on with a nice, solid click. It has a good dimmable range, from a soft night light level to a full room (or tent) level of light.

The best feature is that it uses standard 18650 Li-ion batteries. I am so tired of battery powered items that have non-removable batteries since, when the battery eventually fails, you have to toss the item. With this, you just have to replace the 18650 cells when they will no longer hold a charge well. Plus, since I always have charged 18650 cells for other items, when the batteries run down I don't have to wait for the lantern to charge -- just swap out the batteries for a freshly charged set and you're back in business.

The batteries can be charged without having to remove them (there's a USB C port on the lantern body with a single LED charge light indicator) but, as with any 18650, it's best to charge them in an external charger. The cells claim to be 2400 mAh, but that's somewhat optimistic -- I get a bit less than 2000 mAh capacity when I discharged and metered them. The internal charge rate is 0.6A -- a bit slow, but ideal for good battery longevity.

My only quibble is that I would have liked if the included batteries were from a major brand, such as Sony/Murata, Samsung or LG. But the ones included have been performing fine since an LED light is a pretty low-demand task for an 18650 cell.

A good performing, good looking light that you won't have to toss when the batteries reach their end of life. Five stars and a good value for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Tresda Camping Lantern Rechargeable, 370LM Dimmable LED Vintage Battery Powered Lanterns, Waterproof LED Retro Camping Lights for Camping, Power Outages, Hurricane, Outdoors, Home Décor

text_fidelity_a: Razor A4 Kick Scooter OK, so I had to have one of these contraptions.  Both my kids had Zootrs for Eco Challenges and tootling around Chicago but I was going to use mine for exercise.  Good choice since cleaning out a clogged sewer ranks above running and biking on my list of druthers. My initial considerations were finding one for an adult weighing more than 90 pounds and costing less than $300.  This seemed to be about the only one.  Had just purchased a motorized Razor (300) for my daughter to ride back and forth from the train station and was very impressed with its quality. However, the size and weight of my new Razor A4 kick scooter surprised me. It's a trick scooter and one should seriously consider its handlebar warning stating "this object moves when in use. Take safety precautions."  OK, I just turned 65 and I'm probably not in the target demographic group, but I'm getting pretty good on it and look less like an idiot every day.  Caution though because the standing area is short and narrow and I have big feet so I tend to switch legs a lot while using the opposing leg for propulsion.  The wheels are tiny and buck whenever they hit a piece of gravel or a twig.  The "trick" is avoiding obstacles in the street.  Have fun.  It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks.  I'm going to borrow one of my kids' Zootrs though and save the Razor A4 for exhibition!
text_fidelity_b: Razor A4 Kick Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Hydraform Reservoir Cleaning Kit I'm pretty frusted with this cleaning kit. Previously I've used CamelBak reservoirs and their cleaning it so everything is in comparison.

For Osprey, opening is slightly smaller which means I cannot fit my hand inside reservoir to scrub inside of it. The brush fits but you really can't get any elbow grease going with it.

For both Osprey and Camel - the dang flexible tube brush is SHORTER than the tube. I just don't get this. It's 5-10 inches too short. Either sell a brush slight longer than half the length, forcing users to go in from both ends. Or, sell a brush slightly longer than the whole thing.So it can be cleaned completely in one fell swoop. Instead of forcing me to use an awkwardly long brush that still needs to be stuck in from both ends.

For Osprey - it is MUCH harder to detaching drinking tube from reservoir so this discourages proper cleaning and too short brush leaves 5 or so inches of disgusting goo left in drinking tube.

For Osprey - the drying rack thing really doesn't fit in reservoir. I forced it in during first use and then really, really struggled to get it back out. Now I only stick it in 3/4 of the way - because at least I can get it back out that way. The plastic is super cheap and every time I bend it it looks very fragile. I can imagine this lasting in real world camping conditions where its going to be exposed to extreme heat and UV light. Mine lives in my kitchen so doing ok so far. CamelPak's 'wings' design is far superior.

Mesh bag it comes in. Pretty snazzy but so form fitting no one is going to use this again to hold the cleaning kit because it is such a tight fit - could be used as a stuff sack for something else - maybe eating ware??

So overall - just awkward to use because there were a million ways to better design this especially when CamelPak is just sitting there with obvious design improvements. But still, mostly it works and is better than trying to use non-custom brushes for same purpose.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Hydraform Reservoir Cleaning Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Renegade GK Talon Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 5-11, 5 Styles, Level 3) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 3.5+3MM Hyper Grip XD | Durable Goalkeeper Glove for All-Around Play | Based in The USA Update, 1 Let me say customer service is a 5 Star easily, prompt, courteous, and willing to make it right. We are well into our second pair of gloves at this point (got them in AUG, now Dec), and they have held up much better. However, the sticky factor is long gone as the material doesn't seem to keep that aspect. I purchased a bottle of GloveGlu which has fixed that issue.

I have increased the review to three stars, had the initial pair of gloves been as good as the second pair this would be a 4 star review. I think it odd, that the "pattern" in these reviews is the first pair of gloves tend to be less than quality, and then the second pair meets expectations. I would suggest that whoever is "making" the gloves need to improve their quality inspection as they gloves do not seem to be meeting the owners expectations, and it can't be good for the bottom line of the company to continue to reissue new gloves and give discounts on the original purchase to make it right. We purchase a new set every year, if the product would have had the quality of the second issue, I would have bought next years set from this company; however, given the pattern of the reviews, that may not be the case.

Once again customer service was 5 star, in the end the review is about the product, customer service should have never been involved nor a second pair of gloves. That combined with the pattern of the reviews, I feel 3 star (for this experience) is justified.

A bit disappointed in the gloves, we bought on May 18th it is now July 24th and they seem to showing signs of wear already the last set of gloves didn't show for 8 months or so. They also do not seem as "sticky" as the previous pair.

With that said my 11 year old plays year round both indoor and out, uses the gloves three times a week for practice plus 1-2 games a weekend. Seems as if he is dropping more balls than he use to as they gloves don't seem to have kept their grip. So now I am stuck with either paying $15 - $30 bucks for some glove stick or applying that amount toward another pair of gloves 2 months after these were purchases.

All in all fairly disappointed in the gloves.

UPDATE: WOW! What Customer Service, within two days of this post, I heard from the owner of the company who believed the gloves could have been defective AND he sent overnight a new pair so my son would have them for his weekend games.

I am certainly eager to see how the new set of gloves wear this go around and really hope they are as good as the customer service. Will Update later.

I'm a 5'5" female, about 145#. I got the small and it fits perfectly.
As others have said, it's somewhat bulky in the front, which I suppose is to ensure you float face-up. Given the large arm openings, I don't THINK this will negatively impact paddling movements. I will report back after I've used. (Weather may delay...)

It's a short vest, which I like. It allows room for the back of the kayak seat to fit under the vest.
I think the mesh openings will help allow airflow and keep me cooler than a more solid vest.

Tepui Camp Lounge Furniture Lawn chairs are useful for many purposes. They come in handy when you attend events and are a practical addition to your backyard. They are not all created equally, though, and one of the better ones I have used is this chair, the Tepui Single Chair.

Taken from its transporting bag, this lawn chair is ready to use- you just have to pull the legs apart and stand it up. It has a cup holder for drinks and I like that it is placed below the chair, attached to the leg. With other lawn chairs, the cup holder is right there, on the arm of the chair, and your drink can get in the way of resting your arm. I also like that the covers on each arm are removable. They are held in place with Velcro and if you don’t prefer them, that is perfectly fine, as they are easy to remove.

With comfort, this chair is better than most. I don’t get that ‘sinking feeling’ like I often do with other lawn chairs. This one feels more secure and the weight limit rating confirms that it is, indeed, stronger than the average lawn chair. Another cool feature is the mesh back. It allows air to flow through and it does make a difference at keeping you cool and preventing perspiration from forming on your back.

This lawn chair is easy enough to fold back up and place into the carrying bag when you’re finished. I should point out that this chair is heavier than others so carrying it for a long distance could be tiring. However, it is also stronger and more durable than others. I am willing to put up with the added weight to have a better lawn chair.

I have several different lawn chairs for home and event use. This lawn chair from Tepui is an excellent one overall, delivering on comfort, quality, and strength. It is the best lawn chair I currently own and now that I have used it a few times, I am ready to toss my other, cheaper chairs in the trash and replace them all with this one. It really is that good!

Cat Caterpillar Camo Hydration Reservoir -2L We don't hike per se, but we do head out to the ranch in the deep West Texas borderlands a couple of times a year and you absolutely need water on your person out there. The Chihuahua desert and Chinati mountains combined with extreme temperatures out there can cause a serious hydration problem very quickly. Typically, I put two one gallon containers per person in our saddle bags and we ride out. I like the idea of having this water pouch for walking with it's built in straw.

The pouch itself is easy to see with clear sections in the camo print so you know exactly how much water you have left. The straw has a pull off cover and it pops back into place with a firm click so you know it's really closed. My problem is the lack of velcro or any sort of straps to attach it to a backpack or belt. Basically, you have to carry it or already have a backpack with existing straps or a pocket available to hold a water pouch. It this had an attached loop even on the top, I could clip it my saddle or my jacket - I rarely use a backpack when on horseback so we'll have to retrofit something to this.

I filled up the 5 liter one to see what it was like. The plastic is very thin. I was afraid it might burst as I was filling up. It wouldn't hold itself up until it was full. When it's full, water leaks out of the valve from the pressure. Maybe I over filled it, though. I didn't measure the water going in.

After the water level went down, the valve stopped leaking. I put it on the floor and after a few days, I realized that water was slowly spreading across the floor. I put it in a big stew pot (perfect fit) and it continues to slowly leak but not that much. I think the water is actually coming through the plastic but I can't really tell. It will do for an emergency.

If I ever fill up the 15 liter ones, I think I'll have to put them in the bathtub first. I'd be afraid that they might burst and flood my apartment. If you plan to use them for camping and such, I'd pay more for a better quality and thicker plastic.

text_fidelity_a:
LuxFit Ball Chair, Premium Fitness Exercise Ball Chairs for Home and Office 2 Year Warranty! with 2000lbs Static Strength Ball Great Office Desk Chair, and Stability Ball Chair I have been using this chair for a few weeks at my desk at work. I like it. As someone who is fairly fit and does an hour of ab work most weeks, I honestly can't say that I notice a drastic difference in my ab toning or how my abs feel after using this chair for hours a day. The difference I can notice is in my posture. My back used to hurt so much because I got in the bad habit of crossing my legs and leaning to one side, one forearm bracing my body using one arm of an office chair. Ouch. I knew I had to eliminate a stable backrest and armrests to retrain my posture, and I wanted to challenge my seated body more than in a basic office chair.

All around, this is a great chair. I love the rolling feature. I followed a suggestion of another reviewed to inflate to about 12", wait a day, then inflate further. It worked. Fully inflated, the height is 23", which is what I needed. I am 5'4" but my computer screen is mounted high off of my desk. The backrest is almost useless at my height, to be honest. I would never sit so far back in the chair to have my back touch the rest. Sometimes if I have been seated for several hours, my upper back will begin to hurt out of strain, so I will lean far back for a few moments. Also, it is good to use to stretch if twisting. If I had known what I know now, I would have opened my search to models without backrests. Alas. This chair is fine.

Women: I wear dresses that hit 1-2" above my knee most days. I had no problem sitting on this chair. I work in an enclosed L-shape desk and I have spread my legs a little when sitting in this chair, but I haven't found it absolutely necessary or most comfortable. I can see how you gain great stability with widespread legs, but I'm most naturally inclined to have my legs straight in front of me. I can easily meet with someone seated across from me with my legs closed without feeling unstable. The one caveat to this is high heels-- I'm not talking about 1" wedges, but 2"+ and pointies-- it will be less sturdy to navigate and you may feel compelled to spread your legs to gain your balance.

Additional info from several months of use: You definitely expend more energy sitting on this bad boy. I came down with the flu and my first day back in office I sat down for a few moments and knew I wasn’t strong enough to stay in this chair.
text_fidelity_b: LuxFit Ball Chair, Premium Fitness Exercise Ball Chairs for Home and Office 2 Year Warranty! with 2000lbs Static Strength Ball Great Office Desk Chair, and Stability Ball Chair

text_fidelity_a:
Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer) We have three sets of kitchen knives; a low quality TV infomercial special, a medium quality Chicago Cutlery set, and what we consider high quality home knives by J.A. Henckels. Plus we have more working knives than I care to count. I have used a lot of sharpeners and edge straighteners over the decades but we only use those now for machetes that my wife won't let me use in the Chef's Choice 120. They'd fit too!

I bought the 120 for my wife two years after I bought her the J.A. Henckels knives. New, the knives were amazing; felt like they had a near surgical edge. I knew once they got dull or burred we didn't have anything that would restore them to like-new condition. Before we bought the 120 we took our dull Chicago Cutlery knives to a professional butcher for sharpening to see what we'd get back. We were not impressed with the results so I knew we needed to find a good knife sharpener.

After reading the reviews on sharpeners, I chose the Chef's Choice 120. We carefully read the directions and practiced our technique on the cheap knives. Wow, talk about impressed with the results. Then we put the dull Chicago Cutlery knives through all three stages on the 120. Several of the knives were so dull we had to three-stage them three times to recover the edge. When we were finished they sliced effortlessly through paper! They had NEVER been that sharp, even new. They are decades old knives and I will admit the 1st stage of the 120 did put some scratches on the blades about 1/4" up from the edge, but we didn't care. We just wanted a razor sharp edge on the old knives and the 120 delivered.

We tested stage two and three on some loose knives we had to see if those stages scratched the knife blade. They didn't. Most knives that are maintained properly only require stage two and three, or only stage 3. Once we were confident of no scratches we used only the Stage 3 polishing strop stage on the newer J.A. Henckels. Although the knives were two years old and still exceptionally sharp, they had not been sharpened since we bought them. Plus they had developed a few small burrs. The 120 Stage 3 strop stage removed the burrs, restored the near surgical, like-new edge, and no scratches either. My wife was thrilled with the results!

We use the Stage 3 strop stage on several serrated knives we own and they are noticeably improved and shaper. I've used the 120 on my working pocket knives too. I thought they were acceptably sharp using a diamond edge straightener but the 120 takes sharpening to a completely new level.

The 120 will get hot sharpening a bunch of knives one right after the other, but we typically limit our sharpening to ten knives or less. Stage 1 definitely does scratch the blade but that stage is only recommended for hopelessly dull knives.

Others may have issues with the 120. Not us. Once you understand the technique you need to use with the sharpener, it works great! We love it!
text_fidelity_b: Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Colisal Trekking Poles Collapsible Hiking Sticks for Women Men Walking Sticks Lightweight with EVA Foam Grip and Paired with Rubber Tips and Snow Basket Trekking Sticks 1 Pair 125cm I purchased a pair of trekking poles over 15 years ago and paid a lot of money for them. Although I do not use them a lot, I always had trouble with them, particularly getting on the snow/mud basket.

Therefore, when these became available, I wanted to see how they stacked up. These are not heavy duty like the expensive ones but they are still impressive, especially at the $31.99 price point.

They come collapsed as seen in the first photo. I did have some difficulty understanding how to get these to lock in place when fully assembled.  I had to pull down on the top of the pole until the little nub shown in photos three and four popped out. It sort of locks into place like an umbrella locks with the nub.

Once the pole is assembled, which is really quick to do once I figured out how to lock it, then it has to be adjusted to height. The clasps above the nub (photos three and four) opens to  relieve the tension on the telescoping pole in order to make the height adjustments.

All that is left to do is to cinch the wrist strap with enough room to hold on to the poles yet also allow one to release them. The strap locks into place with a plastic piece in the handle once the desired wrist width is reached.

I have no plans to collapse these poles again but that can be done if necessary. I got these for  my boyfriend and he loves them. He walked with them already. He just has to get use to using poles on a hike or walk.

Note that these poles come with a mud basket that can be screwed on (photo five) or it can be used without (photo six).

For the price, these are a good, lightweight alternative to the expensive ones and they are collapsible which makes them more portable than the other poles.
text_fidelity_b: Colisal Trekking Poles Collapsible Hiking Sticks for Women Men Walking Sticks Lightweight with EVA Foam Grip and Paired with Rubber Tips and Snow Basket Trekking Sticks 1 Pair 125cm

The hat itself is lightweight, comfortable, and breathable. The brim really does fold so you can stuff the hat in a bag without it taking up a lot of space. I was worried the brim wouldn’t be stable when wearing the hat, but the fold lines actually help the brim curve and provide better light blocking.

The hat is not adjustable in the normal sense, you can’t make it tighter. The back band is elastic, not a sliding buckle.

The mesh portion to protect the face and back of the neck is somewhat flimsy, and honestly, I am worried how much sun it actually blocks. The mesh is transparent, I can see my face underneath it. So I still put on sunscreen.

I did discover the mesh portion can be stuffed inside the hat and I can still wear the hat on my head. So if I needed the mesh and then didn’t need it, I can just hide it away in the hat and not worry about losing or unsnapping it.

Grizzly Coolers IceDivider | Ice Pack Cooler Divider Update, used with my Kenia 65 cooler other day, it worked wonders, as the cheap ice I used started to melt this divider helped to refreeze the ice on the bottom of cooler. This helped make my ice last even longer. After 4 days of use it finally thawed. I did how ever notice it didnt seal to bottom of cooler. Meaning water will get to the other side as ice melts. So if your using the divider for dry side wet side it isnt going to work. You will have to make some type of seal between the two sides to have any chance of keeping 1 side dry.
But if your using just to help ice stay froze longer this is so perfect for that use.

I love my cooler and it will pay for itself within 40 days of using just off the ice savings.

This worked perfectly for my new 65 quart Kenai Cooler.. apperently the Grizzley Company owns Kenai as well judging by the pamphlet provided with cooler, so there wasnt much research needed to find one to fit.

There is a few lbs of weight (unfrozen) for it to be less then an inch thick, it's also very rugged, I'm sure it could take a drop or two and shouldnt have any issues. It fit perfectly inside the center divider groove and has about 1.5" left from top inside lip.
There is a drain plug on the ice pack for replacement liquid. The pack is thin enough it will freeze pretty quick but it does have some size to it so freezer space may or could be an issue. This will help to precool your cooler before use so you can get the maximum duration of chill out of you high dollar purchase and use it to keep you cup ice seperate from chilling ice that hands, cans touch everytime its opened.

text_fidelity_a:
Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, Portable Shade Sun Shelter UPF50+ UV Protection for 4 Person Extendable Floor for Fishing Hiking Camping, Waterproof Windproof(Blue) [[VIDEOID:c0b9fb38604ef1dadcc1046c1f5ea08e]] We grabbed this Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent for our beach days, where I have to be very careful not to overdo the sun. While she'll lay out, onto of time in the water, I try to get under shade when not out there. We do use umbrellas, but have struggled to find ways to provide consistent shade while the sun makes its track across the skies. So when I saw this...

1. It comes in a carrying bag that you'll use to store and, well, carry it. Like all such bags, the fit is tight. You'll pull to get it out, and be tested as with every such bag, and any box you have ever tried to repack things into - it's a chore. But it got in. We'd love to see such bags with another inch or so of space, but... Took two people pulling out, two people putting in. But as you can see in the video, my wife was able to pop it up alone.

2. There is a tie to keep it tight - think that tie around an umbrella. It would be really nice if this tie were another 4 inches, but you deal. It is not attached to anything, so you'll need to keep an eye on it.

3. The materials seem decent overall and the construction also decent. I'd say better than many ground clothes - which are mostly glorified tarps - but not as nice as some tents we've seen. It should give us a few years, or so our fingers will be crossed. Time will tell...

4. There are stakes and things we think are like shelves or pouches for inside the tent. We did not try them. But there are INSIDE the Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, wrapped and stuffed into that bag, so be careful when pulling things out - they are all apart of it, and as you do, you'll need to stuff them back inside. Not sure we'll use them, not sure we won't.

5. As you can see in the video... set up IS decently easy. Now that we've done it, it SHOULD be far easier when we get out to the beach next. My wife did it side-side-side-top and that worked. We talked about top first, but have not tried it yet. Taking it down was very similar, freaky a little easier now that she knew the strength it took and what would happen. Frankly, it's a cool design and works well. There is a "bottom" to it that's mainly a connected piece that you sort of unfold out and sticks out the front for an overlay onto the sand. It's a nice touch. Once out you can lay other ground clothes on it, blankets, whatever, and that should help hold it down. Again, there are stakes, but we did not try for this test.

We are hoping to get to the beach this upcoming weekend - weather permitting - so as soon as we do - if needed, we'd come back to update - but only if things don't go as planned. Not sure on the overall shade coverage, but the short period of time we were out there, the sun was directly over us and it did give us some decent shade. We feel like we'd set this up in combination with the umbrellas for an overall area of protection for me - and while we might leave the umbrellas in place, we'd move this Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent with the sun/shade movement so I don't have to 1. get out of the shade and 2. it seems lighter and easier than unscrewing the umbrellas out of the sand and moving them 2+ times as we often do.

In the end, this seems like a nice option and we are happy to have it. It should work - again, will update if that doesn't happen - and we are happy to have something that already seems very easy to use. Very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent, Portable Shade Sun Shelter UPF50+ UV Protection for 4 Person Extendable Floor for Fishing Hiking Camping, Waterproof Windproof(Blue)

Coleman 316 Series Insulated Portable Cooler with Heavy Duty Latches, Leak-Proof Outdoor High Capacity Hard Cooler, Keeps Ice for up to 5 Days I wanted to get a pretty substantial cooler to use for backyard BBQ's and for transporting a significant amount of food for long trips. I got the 120 qt cooler, which in retrospect was probably a little overkill.

There is a certain simplicity of design with this cooler. The inside is a very efficient use of space - there are no extrusions impeding the space. The cooler itself is quite sturdy and can take a grown man sitting on it. There are also 4 cup holders, but I don't see using these at all. There are two handles to maneuver the cooler, but there are no wheels, which would make it really difficult to move a cooler of this size.

So, I can't imagine bringing this cooler to a beach or to an outdoor event unless it is empty. Good luck trying to transport the cooler full of ice and drinks without wheels. This does fit perfectly in the back of a SUV or truck so it would be handy for a long drive if you need to transport a lot of food. text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO PD-M324 SPD Dual Platform Pedal These are the only pedals of this variety I've tried. I have two pairs. I use these on my "no attachment" vintage road bikes - bikes that I lock up with a cheap cable lock, and if I come out and the bike is gone, I won't even break stride or spend one minute worrying about it. I do ride a lot and I put a lot of miles on a contemporary road bike with Garmin Vector pedals, which are universe away in form and even purpose. That should be enough background to know where I'm coming from.

First, here's what I love about these pedals. I used to ride my ghetto version of a hybrid bike to nearby stores. That bike is just an old, all-rigid Hard Rock MTB on which I put fenders, a road saddle, and Specialized Nimbus tires. It's so slow that even riding a mile and a half to the grocery store kinda bummed me out. But that was the only bike I could jump onto in street shoes. That's how I arrived at this pedal. I put these on my two old road bikes and now that quick jaunt to the store is much more to my taste.

These pedals are easy to clip in/out, set up, operate. I will say that the pedals I took off my disposable old road bikes, PD-M520L, were slightly easier to clip into and had better clearance. So the switch is a compromise. Basically this M324 is a pedal that does two things, but neither quite as well as the pedals that do just one of the things. That's fine with me.

PROS:
cheap
easy
cleats or any other shoe

CON:
heavy
less ground clearance (I touched down once and have since been careful with these pedals)
closer to road pedals than SPD or platform for ease of getting started - i personally have gotten to where i can clip in w/o looking but it's not as confident with pure SPD pedals, where i just mindlessly mash my foot onto the pedal and it works every time

Overall I'd say that if you want a pedal that is a compromise between platform and SPD, this will make just about anyone happy. It's hard to imagine someone with that as their first criterion who also wants high performance. This is the first pedal of this type I've tried and I didn't even bother trying a different model for my second pair - they are plenty good enough. If they are not the cheapest available they must at least be in the running. Really can't go wrong.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO PD-M324 SPD Dual Platform Pedal

text_fidelity_a:
Trudeau Mist 19-Ounce Hydrator Bottle, Breast Cancer Research Foundation Pink I got these hydrators in all four colors, and they are mostly pretty good - but don't last forever. One of the misters was always hard to pump, one mister quit working after about six months, and the dogs chewed the spray-top off a third. After a while, the deployable straw in two of the hydrators started catching inside the bottle top when rotated, but it's not difficult to winkle it out. One does leak a bit, but so do a lot of sports bottles I've encountered. After a while, two started squeaking when water was drawn through the straw.

So they could be better, but right now I don't see anything better out there. They look cool and are the bomb for preventing spills. They are perfect bedside bottles for a guy like me who tosses and turns a bit, and while the mister holds out they have a thousand and one uses. We've used the mister to mist plants, clean glass, and discipline the dogs, though the aforesaid has resulted. Note that while the deployable straw is 1/4" in diameter, the inner straw is smaller, so the hydrator is fluids only - no smoothies or anything like that. It's easy to drop ice in, though.

Handwashing is best. I do occasionally run them through the dishwasher (top shelf,) but that doesn't really clean the deployable straws, which have to be disassembled to be properly cleaned. Gunk seems to build up at the top of the inner straw over time. After removing the cap, you must push the deployable straw down while gently wiggling down the inner straw - once the latter comes off, grasp the base of the deployable straw and pull it out all the way. Putting it back is a little tricky; insert the deployable straw first and push it all the way in, then push the inner straw into it with the diagonal end pointed to the bottom of the bottle. Sometimes you have to adjust the diagonal end so it doesn't lay flat on the bottom.

If they were just a LITTLE more reliable (or cheaper,) I'd have to give them five stars. If anyone knows of anything better with these features, let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Trudeau Mist 19-Ounce Hydrator Bottle, Breast Cancer Research Foundation Pink

text_fidelity_a:
Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

text_fidelity_a:
WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail Who wouldn’t love some great tunes on their golf cart..?!! As a family who owns a golf cart yet, has never golfed a day in our life - we’ve spent the last decade doing nothing but, fun rides and adventures all around our planned community with our kiddos on this toy. Music would only enhance this- and give us golf cart karaoke?!!

Problem is.. this is a one size fits most. But, it didn’t come close to being “most” for us! How.. when we have the same speaker used in the sellers sample photo description- see photo I included..??!! Right from start when trying to attach we had issues.. this has 6 velcro straps coming out of the sides- (picture a big bug with legs!) Zero instructions included and you'd think this would be straightforward.. Trust me, we tried straps forward wrapping around pole and then, backwards just the same- we even went back to description online.. studied the photo and still had no success.

Problems we incurred:

•Straps are not long enough to wrap around the pole and speaker- and have enough length to close on themself. (this is placing the speaker in same spot as advertised!)

•2 of the 3 sets of straps were sewn in backwards- so, if wrapping around the direction they’re attached- The Velcro teeth on x2 straps are on the wrong side. (Equivalent to getting two negative signs together..) hoping this is an error!

•From photo description it appears we are missing a middle extra strap? Photo shows x1 in brown strap thru middle but, we don’t have anything of the sort...??

•This has no bottom support or “shelf” for added protection.. this could lead speaker slide at the bottom if it were to become a loose. Golf carts bounce around a bit and vibration may cause this to slip. So, bottom support would be helpful if not, necessary to protect the speaker from falling down and give the user peace of mind.

•This is missing a simple but straightforward set of instructions.

overall, this may work with a much smaller size speaker- one with hardly any girth.. Even then, it may be hit/miss to get the securely fastened. I’m afraid a smaller speaker may not produce enough sound to be heard over a motorized golf cart and will it stay safe? In leui of listing this “one size fits all/most..” this would be beneficial to list the actual length and dimension of straps so, one can verify speaker sizes that would work! Listed at a price point of $10- this could be a great find.. if, it could be successful. Tbh, It may be safer to invest more solid option to ensure it will fit/function as expected. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.

The two most useful tools (to me) are the fire starter and the saw. However, in a true survival situation everything in the kit will probably prove useful, and some may even make a big difference.

Also useful is the paracord itself. It is not designed for climbing and supporting your weight, but will definitely allow you to lash together a shelter. Viper Showdown Electronic Dartboard Sport Size Over 30 Games with 590 Options Automatic Scoring LCD Display Missed-Dart Catch Band Battery Operated Included Soft Tip Darts with Replacement Points This dartboard is nice enough for the kids to play around with in the playroom.
I like how the darts are stored on the sides of the game. Sounds are okay but you only get sounds when you hit the double, triple, or the bullseye.
I think I like that better because I'm not hearing constant sounds as the kids are playing.
The colors on the board are nice and bright but, it's really hard to see the score with the light they have on this if you're standing back. A brighter light or having a different background color where the scores show might help.
Overall it's a nice simple dartboard game. Tips are plastic and can break but, I know I can easily find replacements. So, not a big deal.
This is something my grandson would love in his house. So, depending on how long this game lasts, I might consider buying his own next Christmas.

RELIFE Exercise Bike with Adjusable Resistance & Comfortable Seat Indoor Stationary Cycling Bike with LCD Monitor Fitness Bicycle with Heavy Duty Flywheel for Home Gym Cardio Workout Machine New Version, Weight Capacity 400LBS We've wanted to get some sort of indoor aerobic equipment, but a treadmill seemed like it would take up too much space. I love that this bike actually seems to be less floor profile space than any treadmill we looked at, and the non-impact exercise of pedaling rather than stepping is more than welcome! The wheels in front mean I can easily push it into the corner of the playroom when not in use, but then wheel it out in front of the TV when we want it.
It was SUPER easy to assemble, most of it comes already made out of the box. You just need to attach the pedals, handle bars and floor supports.
The only thing is that it seems to have a bit of "give", or a slight wobble/creak once I reach a certain speed. Granted, this is a fraction of the price compared to a brand name like NordicTrack, so you can't really compare it to pro gym equipment. Also, I'm around 200lbs so perhaps I notice it more than someone lighter (like my wife, who didn't seem to notice it). For the price, however, I think it is a fantastic value and intend to get a lot of use out of it!
text_fidelity_b: RELIFE Exercise Bike with Adjusable Resistance & Comfortable Seat Indoor Stationary Cycling Bike with LCD Monitor Fitness Bicycle with Heavy Duty Flywheel for Home Gym Cardio Workout Machine New Version, Weight Capacity 400LBS
